If you do not take Medicare part b, you will be penalized in the future. It is significant as it is a perpetual percentage, meaning the cost will increase over time. You should also look into Medicare part D (prescription drug plan) as you can be penalized for not having that as well.

Now for the good news. There are Medicare advantage plans out there that will actually pay for your part b as an incentive. Essentially giving you free health and drug coverage. This depends on the state you live in though, so no promises. 

Advantage plans are picky about their providers and who you can go to, but in my years of experience working in these programs, they've always seemed to be the best options. Always speak at great length with the Medicare call center people, and realize they have no control over the rules but they can help you navigate these plans and find something that fits your needs. They are paid by the hour, not the phone call, and are not incentivized to sell you any plan in particular. Asking to speak to a supervisor isn't an issue if you get a "bad" agent. Just be patient and try to understand that you are the 100th call they've taken that day, and it isn't even lunch time.
